chapter.title: Essential Oils and Resinoids; Perfumery, Cosmetic or Toilet Preparations

page.h1: HTS Chapter 33: Essential Oils and Resinoids; Perfumery, Cosmetic or Toilet Preparations — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Where U.S. Cosmetics & Perfume Are Sold & the Tariff Each Country Charges (HTS Ch. 33) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The 8 largest markets for U.S. cosmetics, perfume, toiletries and essential oils, what each buys, the tariff it charges by product group and the cosmetics notification or registration needed to sell there.
keywords: tariff on US cosmetics by country

intro: Who buys U.S. essential oils, fragrances, cosmetics and toiletries, **what** they buy and **what they charge** on it. The matrix shows each market's tariff on U.S.-origin goods for the seven Chapter 33 product groups, next to the value the U.S. shipped there in 2025; the EU counts as one market because its members share one tariff. Below it, a short profile of each market names the regulator whose notification or registration a product needs before it can be sold. For cosmetics that step, more than the tariff, is usually what takes time; Canada and China are the two markets where the tariff itself went up.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.name: Canada
markets.rule: CUSMA preferential tariff (0% on qualifying U.S. goods), plus Canada's United States Surtax Order (2026): 50% on U.S. perfume, lip, eye and nail make-up and other hair preparations

3301.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3301.29: MFN Free, United States Tariff Free

3302.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026: 3302.10 MFN Free, 3302.90 MFN 5%; United States Tariff Free

3303.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3303.00: United States Tariff Free; 50% surtax from Sept 8, 2026 (SOR/2026-186, Schedule 3)

3304.rate: Free; 50% surtax on lip, eye & nail make-up
3304.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3304.99: United States Tariff Free; 3304.10, 3304.20 and 3304.30 carry the 50% surtax from Sept 8, 2026 (SOR/2026-186)

3305.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3305.10: United States Tariff Free; other hair preparations (3305.90) carry the 50% surtax from Sept 8, 2026 (SOR/2026-186)

3306.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3306.10: MFN 6.5%, United States Tariff Free

3307.basis: CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, 3307.20: MFN 6.5%, United States Tariff Free

profile.headline: Canada is the biggest buyer and the one where the tariff got worse: CUSMA keeps most of the chapter duty-free, but perfume, lip, eye and nail make-up and other hair preparations have paid a 50% surtax since September 8, 2026, CUSMA or not. Skin care, shampoo, toothpaste, deodorant and flavor bases are not on the list.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Fragrance & flavor mixtures (incl. beverage flavor bases) (3302)
profile.tariffNow: Free (CUSMA) + 50% surtax on perfume, lip/eye/nail make-up

regulator.name: Health Canada (Cosmetic Regulations)
regulator.requirement: The manufacturer or importer files a Cosmetic Notification Form within 10 days after first selling a cosmetic in Canada, and ingredients must respect the Cosmetic Ingredient Hotlist; sunscreens, anti-dandruff shampoos and fluoride toothpastes are drugs or natural health products and need a DIN or NPN before sale.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Canada import requirements

markets.name: European Union
markets.rule: EU–U.S. framework zero tariff (Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I 'ex 33': all of Chapter 33 except 3302 10) from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, replacing the EU common external tariff

3301.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33'), from July 1, 2026; CN 2025 MFN 0–2.9% on 3301 29, 7% on citrus oils not deterpenated

3302.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33') covers 3302 90 (MFN 0%) but excludes 3302 10 food and drink flavor bases (MFN 0–17.3%; 3302 10 29 has a 1,400 t zero-duty quota)

3303.basis: CN 2025 MFN 0% on 3303 00; also in Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33')

3304.basis: CN 2025 MFN 0% on 3304 99; also in Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33')

3305.basis: CN 2025 MFN 0% on 3305 10 and 3305 90; also in Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33')

3306.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33'); CN 2025 MFN 0% on 3306 10, 4% on dental floss 3306 20

3307.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I ('ex 33'), from July 1, 2026; CN 2025 MFN 6.5% on 3307 20 and 3307 90

profile.headline: Since July 1, 2026 the EU charges nothing on almost all U.S. Chapter 33 goods, removing its 6.5% duty on deodorants, shaving and bath products and up to 7% on citrus oils; food and drink flavor bases (3302.10) are the exception. France, the Netherlands and Germany take most of the trade.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Fragrance & flavor mixtures (incl. beverage flavor bases) (3302)

regulator.name: European Commission and national authorities (Cosmetics Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009)
regulator.requirement: An EU-based Responsible Person must hold a cosmetic product safety report and product information file and notify each product on the Cosmetic Products Notification Portal (CPNP) before it is placed on the market; cosmetics tested on animals in breach of the EU ban cannot be sold.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: EU import requirements

markets.name: Mexico
markets.rule: USMCA preferential tariff: 0% for U.S.-origin goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; Mexico's MFN rates on cosmetics rose to 25–36% from January 1, 2026

3301.basis: USMCA; Mexico's tariff schedule (TIGIE), MFN 0% on 3301.29 (WITS 2023); certificate of origin required

3302.basis: USMCA; MFN 0–15% on 3302.10 and 5% on 3302.90 (WITS 2023); certificate of origin required

3303.basis: USMCA; MFN on 3303.00 raised to 25% from January 1, 2026 (DOF decree of December 29, 2025)

3304.basis: USMCA; MFN 25% on 3304.99 and 36% on lip make-up from January 1, 2026 (DOF decree of December 29, 2025)

3305.basis: USMCA; MFN 25% on 3305.10 and 3305.90 from January 1, 2026 (DOF decree of December 29, 2025)

3306.basis: USMCA; MFN 30% on 3306.10 from January 1, 2026 (DOF decree of December 29, 2025)

3307.basis: USMCA; MFN about 10% on 3307.20 (WITS 2023) and 25% on 3307.90 from January 1, 2026 (DOF decree of December 29, 2025)

profile.headline: U.S. goods that qualify under USMCA enter Mexico duty-free. That matters more since January 1, 2026, when Mexico raised its normal rates on perfume, make-up, shampoo and toothpaste to 25–36% for countries without a trade agreement, so goods that don't qualify pay heavily.
profile.mainProducts: Fragrance & flavor mixtures (incl. beverage flavor bases) (3302) · Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304)

regulator.name: COFEPRIS
regulator.requirement: Cosmetics must carry Spanish labelling that meets NOM-141-SSA1/SCFI-2012, and the importer or distributor files a notice of operation (aviso de funcionamiento) with COFEPRIS.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Mexico import requirements

markets.name: United Kingdom
markets.rule: UK Global Tariff (MFN); no U.S. free-trade agreement. The 2025 U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal did not change Chapter 33 rates

3301.basis: UK Global Tariff 2026, 3301.29: 0%; no U.S. preference

3307.basis: UK Global Tariff 2026, 3307.20 and 3307.90: 6%; the 2025 U.S.–UK deal did not change it

profile.headline: The UK charges nothing on most U.S. Chapter 33 goods and 6% on deodorants, shaving, bath and room-fragrance products (3307); nothing has changed since 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Hair preparations (shampoo, perms, hair spray) (3305)

regulator.name: Office for Product Safety and Standards (UK Cosmetics Regulation)
regulator.requirement: A UK-based Responsible Person must notify each product on the Submit Cosmetic Product Notification (SCPN) service before it is placed on the market in Great Britain; Northern Ireland follows the EU rules.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: UK import requirements

markets.name: China
markets.rule: China's MFN tariff schedule, plus the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods (since May 2025) and its 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering U.S. Section 301), which apply unless the importer holds an exclusion

3301.basis: China 2026 tariff: MFN 20% on most essential oils, 10% temporary rate on orange and peppermint oil (2026 plan); + 10% on all U.S. goods; + 2019 counter-tariff, mostly 7.5%, up to 27.5% (Announcements No. 3 and No. 4 of 2019)

3302.basis: MFN 15% on 3302.10 and 10% on 3302.90 (WITS 2023); + 10%; + 2019 counter-tariff of 25% or 5% on 3302.10 lines and 20% on 3302.90

3303.basis: MFN 3% on 3303.00 since July 2018 (Announcement No. 4 of 2018); + 10%; + 25% 2019 counter-tariff (Announcement No. 3 of 2019) unless excluded

3304.basis: MFN 1% on skin care 3304.99 (5% on lip, eye, nail and powder make-up); + 10%; + 2019 counter-tariff of 27.5% on 3304.99 (25% on the other 3304 lines) unless excluded

3305.basis: MFN 3% on 3305.10 and 3305.90; + 10%; + 25% 2019 counter-tariff (Announcement No. 3 of 2019) unless excluded

3306.basis: MFN 3% on 3306.10; + 10%; + 2019 counter-tariffs of 20% (June 2019) and 5% (Sept 2019, halved in Feb 2020) unless excluded

3307.basis: MFN 3% on 3307.20 and 3307.90; + 10%; + 2019 counter-tariffs of 20% and 5% unless excluded

profile.headline: China is the most expensive large market: U.S. perfume, make-up, shampoo, toothpaste and deodorant pay about 38% (normal rate, 2019 counter-tariff and the 10% extra) unless the importer holds an exclusion. U.S. sales there fell 24% in 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Fragrance & flavor mixtures (incl. beverage flavor bases) (3302)

regulator.name: National Medical Products Administration (NMPA)
regulator.requirement: Imported general cosmetics must be filed, and special cosmetics (hair dyes, perms, whitening, sunscreen, anti-hair-loss and new-efficacy products) registered, with NMPA before import, through a China-based domestic responsible person.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: China import requirements

markets.name: Australia
markets.rule: AUSFTA preferential tariff: 0% for qualifying U.S. goods in place of Australia's 5% normal rate on most cosmetics and toiletries

profile.headline: AUSFTA makes qualifying U.S. goods duty-free in place of Australia's 5% normal rate on most cosmetics and toiletries; nothing has changed since 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Perfumes & toilet waters (3303)

regulator.name: Australian Industrial Chemicals Introduction Scheme (AICIS); TGA for sunscreens
regulator.requirement: A business that imports cosmetics must register with AICIS before importing, and the chemicals in them must be authorised for introduction; primary sunscreens (SPF 4 or more) are therapeutic goods that must be on the TGA register (ARTG).

3304.basis: Gulf (GCC) common external tariff, MFN 5% on 3304.99 (WITS 2023); no U.S. trade agreement

3305.basis: Gulf (GCC) common external tariff, MFN 5% on 3305.10 (WITS 2023); no U.S. trade agreement

3307.basis: Gulf (GCC) common external tariff, MFN 5% on 3307.20 (WITS 2023); no U.S. trade agreement

profile.headline: The UAE applies the Gulf common tariff of 5% to U.S. cosmetics and perfume; there is no U.S. trade agreement and nothing has changed since 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Makeup, skin care, sunscreen & nail preparations (3304) · Perfumes & toilet waters (3303)

regulator.name: Dubai Municipality (Montaji product registration)
regulator.requirement: Each cosmetic and personal-care product must be registered on Dubai Municipality's Montaji system by a UAE-licensed company before import or sale; registration lasts five years and needs a free sale certificate from the country of origin.

regulator.name: Health Sciences Authority (HSA)
regulator.requirement: The company placing a cosmetic on the market in Singapore must notify HSA before supplying it and meet the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive requirements.

assumptions: Rates are for 2026, one representative six-digit subheading per product group (shown under each cell): Canada from the CBSA Customs Tariff 2026, the EU from the Combined Nomenclature and Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Mexico from its schedule as amended by the December 29, 2025 decree, and the UK from the UK Global Tariff. China, Australia, the UAE and Singapore are WITS/TRAINS MFN applied rates for 2023, the latest year available, with China's 2026 temporary rates where published. National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

The EU is one market: its 27 members share one tariff, and its export figures include every member. Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 zeroes out Chapter 33 from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, except food and drink flavor bases (3302 10); the normal-rate column shows the rate the EU charged before then.

Canada, Mexico (USMCA), Australia (AUSFTA) and Singapore apply 0% to qualifying U.S.-origin goods; the normal-rate column shows the MFN rate for goods that do not qualify. Canada's 50% surtax (SOR/2026-186) applies to the listed U.S. goods whether or not they qualify for CUSMA.

China's cells add three layers: its MFN rate, the 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (the June 2019 rate plus any September 2019 rate, halved in February 2020) and the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods. An importer holding a market-based exclusion (valid until December 31, 2026) pays only the MFN rate plus 10%. A further 24 points of the extra duty are suspended until January 10, 2027.
Rates are import duties only; VAT, GST and excise are left out. Regulatory requirements are summarised for orientation; check the regulator's current rules for the specific product.
